provenance.source_notes: Reference for this template's layout and text came from screenshots the Forza Writer user supplied directly (in-game/in-editor captures), not from any file, image, or asset extracted or downloaded from the game itself or an official tool. Mirror's Edge (2008) doesn't give its city a confirmed on-screen name in the supplied reference, so `jurisdiction` is left unset here rather than guessing one. Sized 520x110mm (the real EU standard plate size, not this file's usual US-shaped PLATE_W/PLATE_H) since the developer (DICE, Stockholm) and the plates' own European/Nordic proportions in the reference screenshots both point to a European size reference being the closer fit, not an American one -- flagged as an explicit judgment call, not a confirmed in-game measurement. The passenger-car plate shows a green band down the left edge and a barcode filling nearly the whole remaining plate -- no separate readable text is visible at the supplied screenshot's resolution, so this template has no text field beyond the barcode itself. A third, police-vehicle plate variant exists in the game but the user hasn't been able to get a clear look at it yet (no screenshot supplied) -- not modeled here; add it once real reference exists rather than inventing one. The barcode is approximated as a run of '|' characters through the ordinary metrics-based layout pipeline (see glyph_resolve.py's module docstring), same as every other barcode-style template in this set.
